chain.label: unauthorized overspeed warning horn cut-out switch installed
chain.trigger: N125NE was equipped with an overspeed warning horn cut-out switch, an unauthorized modification.

chain.label: marginal high-Mach controllability: Mach tuck, aileron buzz/snatch, nosedown spoiler moment
chain.trigger: the aircraft's marginal controllability characteristics when flown at and beyond the boundary of its high altitude speed envelope

chain.label: cruise at FL430 in narrow 'coffin corner' buffet margin over open water
chain.trigger: the aircraft's operational envelope, therefore, becomes restricted under conditions of high altitude flight because of the buffet boundary limitations

chain.label: inconsistent flight manuals and training on spoiler use for overspeed recovery
chain.trigger: the inconsistencies in aircraft flight manuals and flightcrew training programs regarding the use of spoilers to regain control

chain.label: copilot flying was unrated in the Learjet with only 65 hours in type
chain.trigger: The copilot, who occupied the left seat, was not rated in the Learjet and had limited flight time in this aircraft. It is believed that the copilot was flying the aircraft when a loss of control occurred.

chain.label: weather briefing contained no forecast or warning of clear air turbulence
chain.trigger: There was no forecast of turbulence in the flightcrew's weather briefing.

chain.label: autopilot altitude hold left engaged into turbulence contrary to AFM
chain.trigger: the altitude hold mode of the autopilot was probably engaged when the aircraft penetrated the turbulence... the flightcrew should have had this feature disengaged during penetration of known turbulence to prevent the possibility of a mistrim condition

caused_by.evidence: Because the flightcrew was not alerted to the possibility of encountering clear air turbulence in the weather briefing, the altitude hold mode of the autopilot was probably engaged

chain.label: unexpected encounter with moderate to severe clear air turbulence at FL430
chain.trigger: an unexpected encounter with moderate to severe clear air turbulence

caused_by.evidence: There were no forecasts for clear air turbulence included in the 0900 area forecasts issued by the Forecast Offices at Miami and New Orleans.

chain.label: turbulence upset: aircraft departs FL431, begins right turn and rapid descent with speed increase
chain.trigger: At 1203:46, Jacksonville radar showed the aircraft had lost 300 feet... Cross City radar showed the aircraft had lost 800 feet which computed to about 4,000 feet per minute

caused_by.evidence: the first sign of significant flightpath deviation occurred about 1203:41... when the aircraft began turning to the right and descending from FL 431
the copilot could have been confronted with a mistrim condition... because of the possible nosedown trim the autopilot may have used to counteract the increased airspeed caused by the turbulence

chain.label: inadvertent disengagement of autopilot and yaw damper via wheel master button / force sensor
chain.trigger: since the wheel master button was inside the copilot's left hand grip... it is probable that he could have accidentally disengaged the autopilot and yaw damper

caused_by.evidence: In a sudden upset, a pilot would reactively grab the control wheel in an attempt to maintain control of the aircraft.
The absence of these critical items under these conditions would have significantly contributed to the copilot's difficulty in controlling the aircraft.

chain.label: no Mach overspeed aural warning sounded because horn was cut out
chain.trigger: The lack of the Mach overspeed warning sound on the ATC tape probably indicates that the warning horn was disabled because of the cut-out switch.

caused_by.evidence: In the OFF position, the horn was inhibited.

chain.label: crew failed to recognize overspeed and misperceived upset as a pitch control malfunction
chain.trigger: the upset could have been perceived as a control malfunction. The pilot's statement... 'pull the circuit breaker,' supports this possibility. This possible inaccurate perception of the sudden upset also could have delayed the crew's correct response

caused_by.evidence: the absence of an overspeed warning that probably delayed the crew's response to the turbulence encounter
Since the aircraft's reactions would have appeared very similar in either a turbulence encounter or a control malfunction occurrence

chain.label: no timely thrust reduction after the upset
chain.trigger: the primary reasons for the accident flightcrew's failure to recover were the lack of a timely thrust reduction

caused_by.evidence: Not until 20.4 seconds after the burst of static is there recorded evidence that the flightcrew took action to correct the overspeed condition

chain.label: aircraft exceeds Mach limits in a steepening high-speed dive
chain.trigger: all of which resulted in the aircraft exceeding its Mach limits

caused_by.evidence: thrust must be reduced immediately to recover the aircraft
the pull force will continue to increase as speed increases because of the pitch instability due to Mach tuck
an inadvertent disengagement of the autopilot and yaw damper

chain.label: aileron buzz/snatch buffeting beyond MMO transmitted through airframe
chain.trigger: the staccato sound probably was associated with aileron buffeting at high Mach numbers and that this buffeting was transmitted through the airframe

caused_by.evidence: Aileron 'buzz' onset occurs just above MMO; at higher Mach numbers and/or higher load factors, aileron 'snatch' (rapid, large deflection aileron motion) occurs.

chain.label: pilot commands spoiler extension at high Mach, contrary to Model 25D procedures
chain.trigger: the pilot stated, 'put out the spoilers'... the procedures for the Model 25D/F AFM do not provide for the use of spoilers in this situation

caused_by.evidence: Not until 20.4 seconds after the burst of static is there recorded evidence that the flightcrew took action to correct the overspeed condition when the pilot gave the command to use the spoilers.
the inconsistencies regarding the use of spoilers in training for an overspeed condition may have been responsible for the different response to the upset

chain.label: copilot pulls abruptly on control wheel, exceeding 1.5 g and worsening Mach buffet
chain.trigger: his attempts to recover the aircraft by pulling on the control wheel probably resulted in a loss of roll control

caused_by.evidence: aileron 'buzz' would be the first indication of encountering a high speed Mach buffet condition
extension of the spoilers would have further aggravated the situation by significantly increasing the pull force needed to restore the aircraft to level flight
since he lacked experience in the Learjet, the copilot may have been more aggressive in his response to the upset
Increased load factors caused by manuevering, such as pull-ups or level banked turns, however, reduce the buffet-free speed range.

chain.label: progressive loss of control in an uncoordinated roll from which recovery was impossible
chain.trigger: a progressive loss of control from which recovery was not possible

caused_by.evidence: he was attempting to pull on the control wheel to recover the aircraft but that it was in an uncoordinated roll manuever from which a recovery may not have been possible
the aircraft was diving at high speed and at a progressively steeper angle

chain.label: aircraft crashed into the Gulf of Mexico and was destroyed
chain.trigger: N125NE crashed into the Gulf of Mexico... The aircraft was destroyed by impact forces.

caused_by.evidence: the nature of the damage suggested that the impact was severe

chain.label: both flightcrew members fatally injured; accident not survivable
chain.trigger: The accident was not survivable. Fatal 2

caused_by.evidence: the flightcrew was not found
